continuation_guard.next_required_action: Start B1: declare windows in herdr-plugin.toml.

test_baseline.windows_git_bash: 1 failure at tests/smoke.sh:245 (chmod 500 cannot make a directory unwritable on Windows); all other cases pass

acceptance.criterion: `herdr-plugin.toml` declares platforms linux, macos, and windows.
The action id stays `open`, the pane id stays `helper`, the pane title stays `Lantern`, and the placement stays `tab`.
`herdr plugin action list` reports windows in the action platforms after relink.
`bin/herdr.cmd` forwards its arguments to the POSIX wrapper through `sh.exe` and exits with the wrapper's exit code.
A mutating command through `bin/herdr.cmd` without `HERDR_HELPER_OK` exits non-zero and prints the `HERDR_HELPER_OK` hint.
An inspect command through `bin/herdr.cmd` reaches the real herdr.
With both files present, Git Bash `command -v herdr` still selects the extensionless wrapper.
`bin/herdr.cmd` never falls through to the real herdr when `sh.exe` is missing.
`lib.sh` has `helper_detect_python`, which rejects a zero-byte candidate and validates each candidate by running it.
`launch.sh` uses the detected interpreter for `bin/goals-floor` and `bin/elves-floor`.
A missing interpreter skips the snapshot and never kills the pane.
`lib.sh` has `helper_native_path`, which converts with `cygpath -w` when cygpath exists and is identity otherwise.
`open.sh` passes the native form to `herdr workspace create --cwd`.
`helper_normalize_root` keeps POSIX form, because `launch.sh:95` tests it with `[ -d ]`.
`helper_resolve_real_herdr` accepts a Windows-style `HERDR_BIN_PATH` and returns a path that runs.
It never returns the plugin's own wrapper.
`helper_extend_user_path` leaves macOS and Linux behaviour unchanged and adds no entry that could resolve bare `bash` to the WSL stub.
The unwritable-state-dir case detects a platform that ignores the permission bits and prints a SKIP line instead of failing.
That case still runs and passes on Linux and macOS.
The suite uses the detected Python instead of a bare `python3`.
The full suite passes under Git Bash on Windows with the plain Windows PATH.
`README.md` documents the Windows requirements: Herdr on Windows, Git for Windows, `C:\Program Files\Git\bin` on PATH, one helper CLI on PATH.
`README.md` gives a Windows equivalent for the `hsh` symlink step.
`CHANGELOG.md` has a 0.4.0 entry covering Windows support and the gate fix.
`herdr-plugin.toml` and the README version line both read 0.4.0.
The linked plugin creates a workspace labelled `🔥 lantern` with cwd `C:\Users\Megan` and a tab named `home`.
`claude.exe` starts in the plugin state workdir and the prompt files are written.
A second open focuses the existing chat instead of seating a second one.
The mutation gate blocks a mutating herdr command from Git Bash and from cmd.

master_acceptance.criterion: Lantern opens and runs on Windows through Git Bash, with no change to macOS or Linux behaviour.
The herdr mutation gate cannot be bypassed on Windows by a native process resolving `herdr` on PATH.
`tests/smoke.sh` passes on Windows under Git Bash and stays valid for Linux and macOS.
`README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` describe the Windows requirements and the release.
